To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The cross section for double diffractive production of Higgs bosons or dijets is given by: $$\sigma_{DD}(H/dijet) \simeq 0.1 \cdot \sigma_{SD} (H/dijet), \qquad \mbox{at LHC}$$

the rate of double diffraction Higgs/dijets production is suppressed by a factor of $1/4$ with respect to the rate of single diffractive production, and that this rate is suppressed by another factor of 1/4 due to QCD radiation.

the rate of diffractive HGG production at the LHC is $\sigma_{HGG}\sim 0.1-1$ fb, and that the rate of Higgs/dijets production in rapidity gaps is suppressed by the survival probability $S^2\sim 0.01$ at the LHC, but can be enhanced by the presence of the Higgs boson
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of Higgs bosons and dijets in double gap events.
double diffraction at the LHC.
the production of a Higgs/dijets in double diffractive events at hadron colliders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the double diffractive production of Higgs and dijets is not a background to the Higgs search in the dijet channel, and that the Higgs production cross section is accessible to the experiment.
the double diffractive cross sections are in agreement with the predictions.

, at least for the LHC, the rate of double rapidity gap Higgs/dijets is large enough that it should be possible to measure it, and the rate is large enough that the signal can be seen over the background.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of double rapidity gap Higgs production is suppressed by a factor of $\sim 10^{-3}$ relative to the inclusive Higgs production rate.
the double diffractive production of a Higgs/dijets is not a good signal to search for new physics.
we find a rate for double diffractive production of a Higgs/dijets that is about 10-100 times larger than the standard model background rate for a Higgs/di-jet mass of about 100 GeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of double rapidity gap production is not negligible, and can be measured at the LHC.
double rapidity gap production is not an effective way of suppressing the large QCD background in searches for new particles.
the rate for dijet production in rapidity gap events at the Tevatron is not negligible.
